## Method and limits
- **Windows.** Trends, sentiment, themes and sources run 2024-06-01 to 2026-06-01 (exclusive), so the last full month is May 2026 [c1]. Entities and geography run to 2026-05-01 (exclusive) [c1]. The gap from 31 May 2026 to today (23 Oct 2026) is 145 days (est.). This deliverable says nothing about June–October 2026.
- **Censoring.** The tool cut the series at 2026-06-01 because newer months are incomplete [c1]. No month in this window is flagged partial [c1].
- **Lanes.** One call on news only. No research-literature lane was used.
- **Match mode.** Counts, sentiment and themes use "mention" matching, so any article naming Boeing counts, including lease deals, military aircraft items and passing references [c1]. The sources and recent/critical panels use the stricter "entity_central" mode [c1]. The two are not interchangeable. Entity identity is not verified [c1].
- **What counts are.** Counts are articles, not unique stories, and syndicated copies are likely included (my inference). Polarity is one label per article, the top-scoring of up to three [c1]. Labels are machine-assigned, and "critical" is not the same as "negative" (critical 95,946 vs negative 68,204 [c1]).
- **Coverage.** The corpus passed row-count floors at 107.1% of expected [c1], but the tool states this is not proof of ingest completeness. Place and entity labels lag the crawler [c1]. Sentiment baseline window is not stated.
- **Cannot answer.** Whether coverage is deserved or accurate; critical-share versus a baseline; tone for the last 145 days (est.); which individual stories drove each month; Boeing executives' coverage; full-window publisher concentration.
- **Interpretation (mine, not measured).** The link between the June 2025 spike and the Air India 171 crash; the re-dated PBS item; and "persistently elevated" as a description of the 1.6x gap.
